paper_title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Conventional artificial neurons separate spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, limiting their ability to model irregular observations. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), a continuous-time primitive for replacing standard neural layers in MLPs, Transformers, and graph neural networks. DAWIN couples spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation and integrates it into a local complex state through closed-form damped evolution, avoiding numerical differential equation solvers. We show that DAWIN generalizes static sinusoidal and memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, derive closed-form gradients, and establish bounded-input bounded-output stability for positive damping and sampling intervals bounded away from zero. An associative Triton prefix-scan implementation, DAWINLinear, uses FP32 accumulation and achieves O(log L) parallel depth for sequence length L. Across 11 parameter-matched tasks covering irregular oscillators, MuJoCo dynamics, pedestrian trajectories, and PhysioNet 2012 clinical sequences, DAWIN outperforms Neural CDE on 9 tasks and ReLU-MLP on 8. It achieves the lowest error on dense clinical dynamics (0.9531 NRMSE, winning across all 10 seeds) and ties for the best mortality prediction (0.9993 AUROC). Shuffling elapsed intervals increases error by 58.2%-77.4% on selected dynamics tasks, versus 0.06% on a time-irrelevant control, supporting reliance on physical timing. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, parallel wave integration accelerates inference by up to 2,630 times over its serial implementation and reduces peak GPU memory by up to 97.6% relative to Mamba in the tested configurations.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Conventional artificial neurons compute memoryless affine projections followed by static pointwise activations, decoupling spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time. When observations arrive irregularly, existing continuous-time paradigms rely on expensive numerical differential equation solvers, separable linear state-space projections, or task-specific sequence blocks that cannot serve as universal replacements for standard linear layers. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), foundational primitive that directly replaces the conventional perceptron across arbitrary neural architectures. DAWIN mxi) and Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) interval unit is atomic because it combines spatial projection (k scaling (αm(ti)) into an indivisible spatiotemporal wave packet, and integrative because it embeds this wave directly into local complex state governed by continuous-time damper evolution operator exp((γm + iωm)ti). We prove that DAWIN strictly generalizes static sinusoidal perceptrons (γm ) as well as memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, derive closed-form backpropagation rules, and establish uniform Bounded-Input Bounded-Output (BIBO) stability for any γm > 0. By proving exact associativity of atomic wave integration, we construct paired-real Triton parallel prefix-scan kernel (DAWINLinear) with FP32 accumulation that executes in O(log L) parallel depth, eliminating serial recurrence bottlenecks. Across 11 parameter-matched tasks spanning irregular oscillators, MuJoCo continuous control, ETH/UCY + JAAD pedestrian trajectories, and PhysioNet Challenge 2012 clinical sequences on NVIDIA B200 GPUs, drop-in DAWINLinear integration achieves best overall accuracy on dense clinical dynamics (0.9531 NRMSE, 10/10 seed wins, < 0.01) and mortality prediction (0.9993 AUROC), outperforms Neural CDE on 9/11 tasks and ReLU-MLP on 8/11 tasks, and demonstrates causal reliance on physical (+58.2% + 77.4% intervention sensitivity vs. +0.06% on negative controls). Simultaneously, it accelerates inference by up to 2,630 over serial wave recurrence and 18.6 802.1 over S5, Mamba, and Neural CDE while reducing peak VRAM by up to 97.6%. Keywords: Continuous-Time Neural Networks, Irregular Time Series, State Space Models, Parallel Associative Scan, Triton Kernels 1 Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN)

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Modern deep learning architecturesspanning multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), Transformers, and graph neural networks (GNNs)share single foundational computational unit: the static artificial neuron = σ(wx + b) [13]. While expressive on static or uniformly sampled data, this primitive fundamentally decouples spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time. When observations arrive asynchronously as in autonomous motion tracking, irregular clinical records, event-driven sensors, and continuous physical controlconventional neurons lack an intrinsic mechanism to represent how latent response should evolve across an arbitrary elapsed interval ti = τi τi1. Practitioners must instead inject ti as an auxiliary input feature, rely on discrete positional indices, or wrap static layers inside specialized macro-architectures. Existing continuous-time paradigms address irregular sampling at the trajectory or sequence-layer level rather than at the atomic neuron level: Differential Equation Solvers (Neural ODEs & Neural CDEs): Continuous-time differential equation models evolve hidden states between observations via numerical integration [2, 9]. Although mathematically principled, adaptive step-size solvers impose substantial sequential latency, complicate backpropagation, and require bespoke solver pipelines that cannot serve as lightweight drop-in replacements for standard linear layers. Structured State Space Models (S4, S5, LRU, Mamba): Modern SSMs discretize continuous linear generators into diagonal or selective recurrences amenable to parallel prefix scans [6, 17, 5]. However, SSMs separate linear spatial input projections (Bxi) from temporal state transitions ( Ahi1), preventing spatial features and elapsed intervals from coupling multiplicatively within an atomic wave packet. Prior Wave Formulations (WFB & WSP): Wave Function Backpropagation (WFB) introduced differentiable wave neuron cos(kxωtθ) that couples spatial input and elapsed time inside single phase, but its feed-forward formulation is stateless across observations [19]. Wave State Propagation (WSP) introduced persistent complex recurrence over measured intervals, yet it decoupled contentconditioned wave injection from layer-level propagation, required rank-reduced conditioning networks, and relied on serial execution that lagged behind parallel Transformers in large-batch throughput [10]. We resolve these limitations by returning to the fundamental building block of neural networks. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), universal, drop-in replacement for the conventional perceptron. DAWIN is built on two unifying principles: 1. Atomic Spatiotemporal Wave Excitation: Each DAWIN unit combines spatial wave phase mxi θm) and ZOH envelope modulation (αm(ti) = 1 eγmti for ti > 0, with αm(0) = 1) into (k an indivisible (atomic) complex wave packet ui,m = Amαm(ti) exp(i(k mxi θm)). 2. State Integration via Damper Activation: Instead of emitting this wave memorylessly, DAWIN integrates ui,m directly into local complex state ψi,m, governed by continuous-time damper evolution operator Dm(ti) = exp((γm + iωm)ti) that rotates and exponentially attenuates prior wave history across ti. Contributions. Universal Continuous-Time Neuron Primitive: We formalize DAWIN and its layer-level interface (DAWINLinear), proving that it strictly generalizes static sinusoidal perceptrons (γm ) and memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, while propagating paired-real quadratures that drop seamlessly into Pre-Norm residual MLPs, Transformers, and dynamic GNNs. Closed-Form Gradients & BIBO Stability Guarantees: We derive closed-form backpropagation rules through irregular intervals and prove uniform Bounded-Input Bounded-Output (BIBO) stability for any strictly positive damping rate γm > 0, ensuring resilience against spatial outliers (xi ) and arbitrary observation dropouts without requiring normalization inside the recurrence. 2 Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN) Multi-Block Fused Parallel Associative Scan Kernel: We prove exact associativity of atomic wave integration and implement three-stage chunked Triton prefix-scan kernel that evaluates DAWINLinear in O(log L) parallel depth across arbitrarily long sequences (L > 4096), eliminating the serial throughput bottleneck of WSP. Cross-Backbone Empirical Validation: We establish standardized 10-seed evaluation protocol across irregular MuJoCo physical dynamics, ETH/UCY + JAAD pedestrian trajectories, and dense/mask-aware PhysioNet Challenge 2012 clinical sequences, demonstrating consistent accuracy and throughput gains over static baselines, prior wave models, Neural CDEs, and S5/Mamba under strict parameter parity.

sections.title: 2.1 Continuous-Time Neural Differential Equations
sections.content: Neural differential equations model irregular time series by parameterizing continuous latent trajectories with ordinary or controlled differential equations. GRU-D introduces heuristic exponential decay on hidden states and missing inputs [1], whereas Neural ODEs and Latent ODEs evolve latent vectors continuously between observations using numerical ODE solvers [2, 12]. GRU-ODE-Bayes and Liquid Time-Constant (LTC) networks integrate continuous flows with recurrent observation updates [4, 8], while Neural Controlled Differential Equations (Neural CDEs) drive latent dynamics via continuous interpolation paths of incoming measurements [9]. ContiFormer extends this paradigm to self-attention by integrating continuous ODE trajectories inside attention keys and values [3]. All numerical ODE/CDE methods require iterative solver steps across each inter-observation gap, incurring heavy sequential overhead and numerical discretization error. DAWIN achieves exact continuous-time evolution in O(1) closed-form operations per event without numerical solvers, operating as an elementary neuron rather than trajectory-level ODE wrapper.

sections.title: 2.2 Structured and Selective State Space Models
sections.content: Structured State Space Models (S4, S4D, S5, and Linear Recurrent Units) demonstrate that continuous-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems h(t) = Ah(t) + Bx(t) can be discretized via zero-order hold (ZOH) or bilinear transforms into parallelizable diagonal recurrences [6, 7, 17, 11]. Oscillatory variants such as UnICORNN and LinOSS further constrain state matrices to second-order harmonic dynamics [14, 15], while Mamba introduces input-dependent selectivity over discretization steps and transition matrices [5]. While the decay-rotation operator exp((γm + iωm)ti) shares the mathematical structure of diagonal complex SSM transition, standard SSMs rely on separable input projections (Bxi) followed by temporal discretization. In contrast, DAWINs atomic wave excitation couples spatial projection mxi and ZOH interval scaling αm(ti) inside an indivisible atomic wave packet ui,m = Amαm(ti)ei(k mxiθm) while evolving phase via Dm(ti) = e(γm+iωm)ti, enabling constructive and destructive interference directly at the neuron level.

sections.title: 2.3 Periodic Representations, WFB, and WSP
sections.content: Periodic activations such as Fourier Features and SIREN establish that sinusoidal functions compactly represent high-frequency spatial fields and their analytical derivatives [18, 16], but they treat time either as static coordinate or via fixed frequency encodings. Wave Function Backpropagation (WFB) introduced learnable wave parameters (A, k, ω, θ) whose phase explicitly incorporates t, demonstrating strong parameter efficiency in feed-forward trajectory prediction [19], yet lacking an internal state across observations. Wave State Propagation (WSP) addressed persistence by introducing complex carry recurrence over measured intervals [10], but was formulated as specialized sequence-modeling block with low-rank conditioning networks and serial execution. DAWIN unifies WFB and WSP into single atomic neuron primitive (DAWINLinear) with formal BIBO stability guarantees, fused parallel associative scan kernel, and universal drop-in applicability across MLPs, Transformers, and GNNs  (Table 1)  . 3 Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN) Table 1: Structural comparison between the conventional perceptron, prior wave formulations (WFB, WSP), and our proposed DAWIN primitive. sections.title: 5 Experimental Design & Benchmarks
sections.content: Our empirical protocol evaluates four Research Questions (RQs) across 10 independent random seeds (101110) under strict parameter-matched budget (2%), spatiotemporal Laplacian regularization (λLap = 104). We use validation-only checkpoint selection and HolmBonferroni-adjusted paired bootstrap confidence intervals (20,000 resamples): RQ1 & RQ2 (Cross-Backbone Universality & Comparator Superiority): Evaluates DAWIN-MLP, DAWIN-Transformer, and DAWIN-GNN against parameter-matched static baselines (ReLU-MLP, TimeTransformer, and GRU-GNN), numerical differential equation solvers (Neural CDE [9]), and structured and selective state space models (S5 [17] and Mamba [5]) across 11 benchmark tasks: (1) controlled synthetic dynamics (damped_oscillator with out-of-range test (0.05, 1.25] vs. train (0.05, 0.50] s, and the dt_irrelevant negative control); (2) irregularly subsampled MuJoCo continuous-control dynamics (HalfCheetah-v5, Hopper-v5, Reacher-v5, Walker2d-v5) [10]; (3) patient-disjoint PhysioNet Challenge 2012 clinical sequences under mask-aware mortality (AUROC), mask-aware 20% holdout imputation (Masked MSE), and 10-channel dense displacement (NRMSE); and (4) agentdisjoint ETH/UCY + JAAD pedestrian trajectories (Tobs = 8, Tpred = 12 at FPS = 2.5) under position-only (2D) and motion-feature (6D) splits [19]. RQ3 (Causal Utilization of Physical Intervals t): Evaluates fixed trained checkpoints under (a) true t, (b) batch-shuffled tperm, (c) constant batch-mean tconst, and (d) zero-interval probing tzero = 0, alongside the dt_irrelevant negative control. RQ4 (NVIDIA B200 GPU Throughput & Memory Scaling): Measures per-batch latency (ms), throughput (transitions/s), and peak allocated VRAM (MiB) across batch sizes {1, 16, 256, 4096} and sequence lengths {32, 512, 4096, 16384} under BF16 autocast (matmul.allow_tf32 = False, cudnn.allow_tf32 = True).

sections.title: 6 Empirical Results & Discussion
sections.content: All experiments execute on NVIDIA B200 GPUs under mixed-precision BF16 autocast (matmul.allow_tf32 = False, cudnn.allow_tf32 = True) with strict FP32 accumulation inside the associative scan recurrence. 7 Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN)

sections.title: 6.1 RQ1 & RQ2: Cross-Backbone Accuracy Under Strict Parameter Parity
sections.content: Table 2 and Figure 1 report 10-seed test performance across all 11 benchmark tasks with every comparator width-matched within 2% of DAWINLinear. Clinical Time Series (DAWIN-Transformer): When embedded inside Transformer backbone, DAWIN achieves the best overall accuracy on PhysioNet-12 (Dense) (0.9531 0.0006 NRMSE), beating every comparator across all 10/10 seeds (Holm-adjusted = 0.010), and ties for first place on PhysioNet-12 (Mortality) (0.9993 0.0015 AUROC), outperforming Neural CDE (0.6974) by +0.3020 (p = 0.010). Irregular Oscillatory Dynamics & Solver-Free Advantage: On Damped Oscillator with outof-range test intervals (0.05, 1.25] s, DAWIN-MLP (0.7589 0.0201) significantly outperforms S5 (0.8177), ReLU-MLP (0.8399), Time-Transformer (1.0604), and Neural CDE (1.2799) across 10/10 seeds (p = 0.010), while matching Mamba (0.7373 0.0539, = 0.190) with 2.7 lower variance across seeds. Across all 11 tasks, DAWIN outperforms Neural CDE on 9/11 tasks and static ReLU-MLP on 8/11 tasks. Architectural Scope & Causal Trade-Offs: On PhysioNet-12 (Imputation), non-causal window flattening (ReLU-MLP, 0.2355) and selective sequence mixing (Mamba, 0.3046) achieve lower masked MSE than strictly causal forward wave integration (DAWIN-Transformer, 0.3655), reflecting the distinction between causal filtering and bidirectional gap reconstruction. Similarly, on continuous control (HalfCheetah-v5, Hopper-v5, Reacher-v5 ) and trajectory forecasting, standalone 2-layer DAWIN-MLP trails global self-attention (Time-Transformer) and input-selective gating (Mamba) in pure accuracy while offering an order-of-magnitude latency and memory advantage.

sections.title: 6.2 RQ3: Causal Utilization of Physical Intervals ∆t
sections.content: Figure 2 and Table 3 summarize test-time interventions on trained DAWIN checkpoints. Replacing true intervals with batch-shuffled tperm degrades test NRMSE by +60.96% on Damped Oscillator, +58.21% on HalfCheetah-v5, +77.43% on Hopper-v5, and +71.95% on Reacher-v5 (with +31.0% + 46.0% degradation under constant tconst). Conversely, on the t-Irrelevant Control, shuffling intervals produces negligible +0.06% shift (+0.0002 NRMSE), confirming that DAWIN exploits physical timing causally without introducing spurious temporal bias.

sections.title: 6.3 RQ4: NVIDIA B200 GPU Throughput and Memory Scaling
sections.content: Table 4 and Figure 3 quantify synchronized CUDA latency, throughput, and peak allocated VRAM on NVIDIA B200 across {32, 512, 4096, 16384} and {1, 16, 256, 4096}: Eliminating Serial Recurrence Bottlenecks: The multi-block Triton associative scan (DAWIN-MLP Parallel) executes = 16,384 (B = 1) in 0.716 ms (22.88 106 transitions/s), achieving 2,629.9 speedup and 54.2% VRAM reduction over exact serial wave recurrence (1,876.51 ms). Order-of-Magnitude Gains Over SSMs, Transformers, and Neural CDEs: At = 512, = 256, DAWIN-MLP (Triton Scan) achieves 75.51 106 transitions/s (1.736 ms, 443.45 MiB)outpacing Time-Transformer by 1.77, S5 by 6.91 (75.2% less VRAM), and Mamba by 58.28 (97.6% less VRAM: 443.45 MiB vs. 18,713.32 MiB). It also runs up to 802.3 faster than Neural CDE (L = 512, = 16).

sections.title: 7 Conclusion, Limitations, and Broader Impact
sections.content: Conclusion. We introduced the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), foundational continuous-time neural primitive designed to serve as direct, architecture-agnostic replacement for the conventional perceptron. By uniting spatial projection and elapsed-time phase evolution into an indivisible wave packet and integrating that wave into local state under continuous-time damper operator, DAWIN 8 Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN) resolves the core limitations of memoryless wave layers and decoupled sequence propagators while scaling in O(log L) parallel depth via fused Triton associative scans. Limitations & Future Directions. Canonical DAWIN units learn fixed intrinsic frequencies ωm and damping rates γm; extending these to bounded input-modulated damping gates γi,m [γmin, γmax] could improve modeling of sharp regime switches while preserving scan associativity. Additionally, spectral band initialization can mitigate phase wrapping when extrapolating to intervals far beyond training ranges, and multi-axis associative scans extend naturally to continuous spatiotemporal PDE operators. Broader Impact. Providing solver-free, drop-in primitive for irregularly sampled data benefits clinical monitoring, autonomous safety, environmental sensing, and robotics while reducing training energy compared to iterative ODE solvers. High-stakes clinical and safety-critical deployments require domain-specific calibration and human oversight.
